drivingQuestion: Must one actually use the flame's light in order to bless over it, or does it suffice that he could use it if he stood close?
outcomeNote: The objection is deflected by rejecting the reading of the Tosefta on which it depended; Rav's position stands.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: לֹא ״יֵאוֹתוּ״ יֵאוֹתוּ מַמָּשׁ, אֶלָּא כׇּל שֶׁאִילּוּ עוֹמֵד בְּקָרוֹב וּמִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לְאוֹרָהּ, וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּרִיחוּק מָקוֹם. וְכֵן אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: בְּרִיחוּק מָקוֹם שָׁנִינוּ.
segments.en: «Rav Yehuda says »that «Rav says: Derives benefit does not »mean that the one reciting the blessing must« actually derive benefit »from the light of the candle. «Rather, as long as if one were to stand close »to the candle «he could utilize its light, »if he sees it he may recite a blessing over it, «even »if he is now standing «at a distance.»

segments.he: מֵיתִיבִי: הָיְתָה לוֹ נֵר טְמוּנָה בְּחֵיקוֹ, אוֹ בְּפַנָּס, אוֹ שֶׁרָאָה שַׁלְהֶבֶת וְלֹא נִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לְאוֹרָהּ, אוֹ נִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לְאוֹרָהּ וְלֹא רָאָה שַׁלְהֶבֶת — אֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ עַד שֶׁיִּרְאֶה שַׁלְהֶבֶת וְיִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לְאוֹרָהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara «raises an objection» from a Tosefta: «One who had a candle hidden in his lap» or placed «inside an» opaque «lamp, or if he saw a flame and did not utilize its light, or if he utilized its light and did not see a flame, may not recite a blessing until he» both «sees the flame and utilizes its light.»

segments.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לְאוֹרָהּ וְלֹא רָאָה שַׁלְהֶבֶת מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ — דְּקַיְימָא בְּקֶרֶן זָוִית. אֶלָּא רָאָה שַׁלְהֶבֶת וְלֹא נִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ לְאוֹרָהּ הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ? לָאו דִּמְרַחֲקָא?!
segments.en: The Gemara first clarifies the content of the Tosefta itself: «Granted,» a case where one «utilizes its light and did not see a flame, can be found where» the flame «is situated» around «a corner,» illuminating the area but hidden from his view. But «how can» a case where one «saw a flame and did not utilize its light be found? Is it not» referring to a case «where one is distant?» Apparently, one must actually utilize the flame; merely having the potential to utilize it is not sufficient.
The Gemara rejects this: «No.» This refers to «a case where» the flame is «gradually dimming.» One sees the flame, but is unable to utilize its light.
